transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03
Time: 15:00 - 15:54 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE); Marcus Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Raman (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Harborly Head of ML); Jordan Li (Harborly VP Eng); Samir Rao (Harborly SRE); Ava Gomez (Harborly Product); plus one dial-in labeled Speaker 1 (possible contractor)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style retro on recent stability sprint, review of usage and costs through the quarter, and alignment on next-phase roadmap and pilot benchmarks. Key themes: tail latency spikes during black friday test, cost drift vs projected, options for Dedicated vs Hosted with VPC peering, and a pilot plan for quantization and KV cache tuning.

Topics covered (auto):
- Recent incidents and postmortem highlights
- Token consumption patterns and cost allocation across environments
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and observed tail spikes
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and private deployment constraints
- Roadmap and next steps for pilot/benchmarks

Action items (summarized above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining. we'll do a quick run through the stability sprint results and then go into cost allocation. i think priya's gonna kick us off with the context.
[00:22] Priya Raman: yep should be quick. hi harbory team, congrats on the sprint, a few incidents but overall improvement on 95th latency vs last quarter. main goals today: agree on pilot targets and share artifacts.
[00:38] Jordan Li: thanks priya, yeah overall better but we still hit tail spikes during the simulated checkout surge friday test, that was the biggest pain. p95 is good but p99 jump to about 1.6s which is a problem for checkout.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: right we looked into the traces, a lot of the p99 is KV cache misses and some tokenization variance. with a better prefix cache hit rate we shaved p99 from 1.6s to around 0.9s in our internal run. note: KV cash to cache—transcript note, the auto text hates cache.
[01:37] Maya Patel: quick Q, what are we seeing on cost side? our FinOps folks flagged a 22% overrun vs the commit for March.
[01:53] Lena Ortiz: we pulled the usage. harborly used ~12.1M tokens across prod+staging for March. cost driver was a mix of a larger temperature config on some flows and fallbacks to the larger model during overloads. also, autoscaling burst configured conservatively—so panics.
[02:26] Samir Rao: autoscale kept spinning up higher GPU tiers; we didn't have the right routing policy to fallback to cheaper model variants. we want to avoid full dedicated spikes.
[02:40] Marcus Chen: exactly; that's where smart routing and model variants help. one option: keep hosted for low-latency storefront queries and route heavy batch day/night flows to a Quantized-Dedicated pool. quantization-wise we tested 8-bit and 4-bit(inf) profiles; 8-bit gave about 1.8x throughput and minor quality changes, 4-bit gains larger but needs more eval.
[03:12] Ava Gomez: are those quality regressions visible to end users? we can't have checkout hallucinations.
[03:20] Marcus Chen: no hallucinations in our evals for the top-of-funnel prompts. for checkout we recommend a hybrid: keep full-precision for payment/PII-related calls and quantized models for conversational assistance. also enforce rerank/verify step.
[03:42] Jordan Li: that makes sense. can you rerun the checkout path with same prompts and token lengths? we need p95 under 300ms ideally.
[03:54] Marcus Chen: under 300ms is ambitious for complex multi-turn context but we can get p95 to around 180-250ms with batching and persistent KV hits on a dedicated A100-ish pool; depends on model seq length. we'll add a conservative config table.
[04:25] Maya Patel: sequence length for checkout is typically 64 tokens, but our support chat flows hit 512 occasionally.
[04:36] Marcus Chen: okay that helps — we can recommend per-route model profiles. small seq for checkout, larger for chat with async fallback.
[04:49] [08:00] Speaker 1: sorry jumped in, question about encryption — your KMS integration, how do keys rotate?
[08:12] Lena Ortiz: good timing — we have KMS integrations with customer-managed keys; rotation policy supports daily rotations via HSM-backed stores; we can share the KMS checklist. (note: sometimes docs say KMS/HSM options).
[08:35] Samir Rao: we need audit logs for all prompt access — retention 2 years. can you confirm export formats?
[08:46] Marcus Chen: yes, audit logs export in JSONL with line-level timestamps, correlate to request id; we also support syslog push to your SIEM. raw prompts can be redacted per route.
[09:10] Jordan Li: what about SSO and RBAC. our infra wants SAML and Azure AD support.
[09:18] Priya Raman: we support SAML SSO integrations and granular RBAC; priya to send runbook.
[09:30] Maya Patel: the security posture is key for our execs — SOC two artifacts and pen test reports?
[09:36] Lena Ortiz: yes SOC 2 Type II. i'll send the pack. quick note — transcript sometimes says SOC two sorry.
[10:05] Marcus Chen: back to latency — we profiled the black friday sim: 1200 concurrent checkout flows, p99 latency spikes tied to KV cache warmup after cold restarts. improving persistent cache warms up reduces tail by ~45%.
[10:36] Samir Rao: any quick wins for us to try before a pilot?
[10:42] Marcus Chen: yes: 1) raise persistent cache retention, 2) enable prefix caching on the checkout route, 3) pin model family for the first 30s of peak, 4) small batch windows for similar seq lengths. these are low-risk config changes.
[11:10] Ava Gomez: on cost allocation — we'd like a per-product cost breakdown not just overall token burn. can Redwood annotate usage by route/model?
[11:20] Priya Raman: yes we have per-route token breakdowns and token-level cost. we can provide a waterfall model that maps cost back to product features.
[11:33] Lena Ortiz: and we'll include committed vs on-demand split.
[11:38] [15:00] Jordan Li: curious about Dedicated: what minimum commit does it make sense for us? we're currently a mid-size e-comm with seasonality peaks.
[15:12] Marcus Chen: typical minimum for Dedicated is monthly reserved capacity — we modeled three scenarios: 4-GPU, 8-GPU, 16-GPU. 4-GPU is cost-effective if steady baseline > ~10 RPS sustained for LP model; 8-GPU is sweet spot for burst headroom. i'll share a spreadsheet.
[15:45] Maya Patel: what about burst capacity? we can't commit to steady 16-GPU but need headroom for promotions.
[15:53] Marcus Chen: Redwood Dedicated supports burst pools and autoscaled burst to hosted tiers with routing policy; you only pay for burst usage at a different rate. that's in the proposal we'll add to the spreadsheet.
[16:20] Jordan Li: how do rollouts work? canary? auto fallback?
[16:27] Marcus Chen: yes canary deploys, gradual ramp with health checks, and automatic fallback to prior model or hosted equivalent on errors. Redwood Console shows per-model traces and token-level cost in near real time.
[16:45] Maya Patel: one of our worries is model version drift — how do you detect quality regressions?
[16:51] Priya Raman: Redwood Optimize hooks eval sets to alerts. we'll run regression alerts against your prompt set and can gate rollouts if NLL/accuracy exceeds threshold.
[17:12] Ava Gomez: what's the on-prem plan in case our compliance team insists?
[17:18] Marcus Chen: Private deployment supports VPC peering and an on-prem package. it's heavier lift but we do support air-gapped installs; need a professional services engagement.
[17:32] Samir Rao: deployment timeline rough estimate?
[17:35] Marcus Chen: for private on-prem, 8-12 weeks typical with FT contracts; VPC-based private can be 3-6 weeks depending on network approvals.
[17:50] [21:00] Maya Patel: back to the sprint retro — the incident had three contributing factors: autoscale misconfig, cold KV warmup, and a rare tokenization edgecase that caused a fallback to bigger model.
[21:20] Marcus Chen: we reproduced the tokenization mismatch — it's due to a pre-tokenizer padding difference in your gateway. fix the pretokenizer alignment and fallbacks stop happening.
[21:41] Jordan Li: we'll get eng to patch the gateway pretokenizer. samir can lead.
[21:45] Samir Rao: yep noted.
[22:05] Lena Ortiz: repository of artifacts: shared deck link (https://redwood.link/harborly-q2-retro-deck), benchmark sheet (https://redwood.link/harborly-benchmarks), and SOC2/ security pack (link to be sent).
[22:34] Ava Gomez: i see item to adjust billing tags so we can attribute to sku and product lines — can that be exported to our billing system?
[22:45] Priya Raman: yes we export cost allocation CSVs and have tagging rules; priya will attach sample.
[23:05] [28:00] Speaker 1: is there support for per-request redaction? sometimes we want to log metadata but not full prompt.
[28:12] Marcus Chen: yes route-level redaction, or token-level redact. we can also store deterministic hashes for correlation without raw prompt.
[28:35] Maya Patel: one open ask from legal — retention windows and right to be forgotten.
[28:42] Lena Ortiz: configurable retention per route; we can also provide deletion APIs and proof-of-deletion logs.
[29:05] Jordan Li: cost optimization ideas: quantization, longer batch windows, prefix caching — which has the best ROI?
[29:15] Marcus Chen: short term: prefix caching and batching are highest impact for request-heavy low-seq routes. mid-term: model quantization. long term: routing policy to cheaper variants and regional routing. i'll rank with rough ROI in the spreadsheet.
[29:46] Ava Gomez: can we see a before/after for p99 and cost if we implement all low-risk items?
[29:54] Marcus Chen: yes — expectation: p99 drop ~30-45%, and cost reduction 18-30% depending on traffic mix.
[30:10] Maya Patel: that's promising. ok next: pilot plan. what would a 4-week pilot look like?
[30:20] Lena Ortiz: week 0: baseline collection and instrumentation; week 1-2: config changes (cache, batching) and small canary; week 3: quantization A/B test on non-PII flows; week 4: performance run and decision review.
[30:40] Samir Rao: for the quant test we need a rollback plan and quick toggle.
[30:45] Marcus Chen: toggle via Console feature flag; instant rollback.
[31:02] [36:00] Jordan Li: any blockers from legal/security?
[36:10] Maya Patel: legal asked for SLA language around p95/p99 for checkout — can we add a carveout for cold start scenarios?
[36:22] Lena Ortiz: yes we can craft SLA with measured exceptions and an incident SLA playbook. we'll draft an Appendix for exceptions.
[36:40] Priya Raman: also recommend a joint incident runbook and alerting thresholds to minimize escalations.
[36:52] Samir Rao: we want daily usage reports during the pilot and fortnightly runbook dry runs.
[37:03] Priya Raman: noted — daily usage for pilot, weeklies for longer.
[37:24] Ava Gomez: final question — is there a recommended token pricing tier if we commit?
[37:30] Lena Ortiz: committed Reserved capacity discounts start at 15% and increase with multi-month and larger commits; we will include modeled rates in the spreadsheet.
[37:48] Marcus Chen: and don't forget burst pricing for hosted fallback.
[38:10] [43:00] Maya Patel: ok to recap, main outcomes: 1) Redwood to share cost/latency models w/ Dedicated scenarios; 2) Harborly to share prompt set & token histogram; 3) Security docs to be exchanged; 4) Setup pilot window and bench run week of Apr 20. anyone disagree?
[43:25] Jordan Li: all good from eng.
[43:31] Samir Rao: good.
[43:35] Ava Gomez: good for product.
[43:37] Priya Raman: i'll follow up with calendar invites.
[43:45] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and the spreadsheet.
[44:00] [49:00] Speaker 1: thanks, quick note that the auto transcript sometimes deidentifies names oddly.
[49:10] Lena Ortiz: yes apologies for any mislabels, we'll attach the raw recording.
[49:25] Marcus Chen: one last technical note — we'll include a recommended autoscaling policy that pins minimal instance count during promo windows; that reduces cold restarts.
[49:48] Maya Patel: thanks, that's helpful.
[50:05] Jordan Li: any ask for our infra team right now?
[50:12] Samir Rao: we'll provide pretokenizer patch and network peering info.
[50:22] Maya Patel: and we'll confirm pilot scope by Fri 2026-04-09.
[50:30] Lena Ortiz: perfect we'll aim to have the spreadsheet and KMS checklist in that window.
[50:38] [54:00] Meeting end — quick thanks and signoff.

Recap (auto):
- Immediate next steps: spreadsheet and security docs; instrument and baseline; pilot week-of Apr 20.
- Risks: cold KV warmup, autoscale configs causing overspend, and tokenization mismatch causing fallback to larger model.
- Recommended wins: prefix caching, per-route model profiles, quantization A/B on non-PII flows, and billing tag exports.
